assignments.brief_reason: Profanity is treated as equivalent to violence and used to justify removal.
Says curse words drove decisions, but does not connect them specifically to threats/violence or mention a moderation-bar rationale.
Uses a rule to reject the whole pair when one side is egregious, but does not primarily describe the pair/mirror fairness standard across viewpoints.
Focuses on removing negativity/attacks to keep opinions while excluding problematic/toxic content.
Profanity and name-calling bias toward removal in favor of non-aggressive, constructive language.
Default to keeping both unless foul language/threats/over-the-top messaging; removal justified by threat/toxicity-type red flags.
Hateful language plus misinformation is treated as a combined reason to remove (toxicity/inflammatory content).
Keep most speech; removal only for extreme sensationalized fake stats or violent calls to action (violence/threat exception).
Tone politeness/absence of insults governs acceptance; this aligns with removing toxic/insulting content.
Vague claim that language influenced judgment without tying to violence/threats or a specific moderation rule.
Wants to check both perspectives, but does not claim same moderation standard across mirror/original pairs.
Uses helpfulness/truth plus a 2nd-amendment lens; not clearly a threat/toxicity-only or cross-side fairness standard.
Mentions checking language/hate speech but also says they avoided judging whose view is right; not clearly matching the violence/toxicity removal themes.
Explicitly blocks content that incites violence (violence/threat exception).
Treats posts as redundant/rephrased and relies on low uniqueness; not a toxicity/violence criterion or cross-side standard.
Assesses whether posts could insult the other side and notes bad actors symmetrically; not clearly a defined moderation-standard or violence-only exception.
Allows both perspectives but blocks obscene/rude/vulgar posts (removing toxic language).
Strong free-speech stance with narrow removals for calls to/coded calls for violence.
Uses 'free speech vs hate rhetoric' as the criterion, but does not explicitly frame it as threats/violence exceptions or specific toxicity-removal standard.
Omits angry/vulgar comments for lack of constructive value—consistent with removing toxic/inflammatory content.
